rics.meaning: Total Labour Force — employed + unemployed. People aged 15+ either working or actively seeking work. From BPS Sakernas.
rics.how_to_use: Indonesia labor force ~143M (2024), growing ~1-1.5% annually with demographic expansion. Labor-force participation rate ~70% (men) and ~55% (women) — female participation gap is a major reform priority.

rics.meaning: Unemployment — total unemployed persons. Same conceptual measure as aIDWKUNTTP.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check series. Indonesia open unemployment ~7.5M (2024). Pair with the rate (aIDUNR) for cycle interpretation.

rics.meaning: Open Unemployment Rate — official BPS unemployment rate. Same conceptual measure as aIDUNR with possible vintage difference.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check series. Use whichever is fresher. Indonesia structural rate ~5%; cyclical bottom around 4.5%; recession peak ~7% (2020).

rics.meaning: Unemployment Rate — share of the labor force without jobs but actively seeking work. Published twice a year by BPS via the Sakernas (National Labor Force Survey), with February and August reference periods.
rics.how_to_use: Indonesia structural unemployment rate around 5-6%. Spiked to 7.1% in August 2020 (COVID) then declined. Underemployment (workers on <35hr/week) is much higher (~25%) — formal unemployment understates labor-market slack. Watch youth unemployment (15-24 yo) which runs 3x the headline rate (~17%).

rics.description: Employment, Labour Force Survey, Standardized (based on source annual data)
rics.meaning: Employment, Labour Force Survey (Standardized) — total employed from BPS Sakernas. Reference labor-market level for productivity calculations.
rics.how_to_use: Indonesia total employment ~135M (2024). Use alongside GDP to compute output-per-worker (productivity). Productivity growth ~2-3% pa — positive but below DM rates.

rics.description: Unemployment Level, % month on month, Standardized, Chg P/P
rics.meaning: Unemployment Level, month-over-month change — but Sakernas is biannual so MoM is interpolated.
rics.how_to_use: Use the level (aIDCUNPP) and YoY (aIDCUNPYP) for primary analysis. MoM has limited signal value given the underlying biannual data.

rics.description: Unemployment Level, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
rics.meaning: Unemployment Level, year-over-year change — pace of unemployment increase or decrease.
rics.how_to_use: Track for cyclical labor-market dynamics. Sharp YoY rises (>10%) signal recession-like conditions. Indonesia rarely shows such moves outside crisis (1998, 2020).

rics.meaning: Unemployment Level (Standardized) — total unemployed persons in standardized framing.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check against aIDUEMP/aIDWKUNTTP. The standardized version aligns with ILO methodology.

rics.description: Unemployment rate, Standardized (based on source annual data)
rics.meaning: Unemployment Rate, standardized (annual) — OECD-comparable framing of the BPS unemployment rate. Used for cross-country comparisons.
rics.how_to_use: Use the headline aIDUNR series for domestic analysis; this standardized version aligns with ILO methodology for international benchmarking. Indonesia's rate has been falling structurally from ~10% (2005) to ~5% (2024) as the labor market absorbs young workers.
